minutes.headline: Water commissioners heard residents on a proposed district expansion on Bird Street; no petition filed, no vote, and a lead line grant item was signed.
minutes.summary: Most of the meeting was a public hearing on H2 Properties' request to expand the water district to a roughly 51-acre site on Bird Street, with residents raising contamination, PFAS, well and water-supply worries. The board explained that the formal petition has not yet been submitted and that any expansion needs a vote of the district. After the public left, the board approved prior minutes, discussed well and water main work, and voted to let the superintendent and chair sign the lead service line program paperwork before adjourning.

public_comment.topic: Resident across from the site opposed expansion, citing past waste pits, bedrock contamination, open DEP cases, and asked the board to wait a few months before calling a special meeting.
Landowner said they spent nearly five hundred thousand dollars on cleanup, face annual PFAS testing costs, and that town water would help close the DEP cases.
Co-owner said they have followed all DEP regulations for 18 years and public water would solve the one contaminated well.
Asked whether water lines could be contaminated passing through polluted soil.
Asked about sewage and leach fields for the development.
Asked the developers about their building experience and schedule, and later about water capacity and PFAS.
Asked whether any preliminary plan or sketch could be shared, noting Zone B zoning.
Resident raised health concerns about pipes through contaminated soil and asked for scientific evidence.
Asked whether water use from the development would be evaluated and affect private wells outside the district.
Opposed the project, citing neighborhood character, wildlife, a new road being torn up and who pays for the pipe.
Concerned about disturbing contaminated soil, her deep well, water use, and that nothing binds the developers to the proposed numbers.
Asked why the water district is the first stop before a defined proposal exists.
Said 4 PM meeting time is hard for working residents.

budget_items.what_was_said: Landowners said the cleanup cost them close to this amount over the years.
figures_as_heard: just shy of five hundred thousand dollars

budget_items.topic: Annual PFAS testing expense for landowners
budget_items.what_was_said: Landowners said testing costs this year are expected to be a large drain on retired owners' savings.

budget_items.topic: Mass Ave water main pipe, ductile vs plastic
budget_items.what_was_said: Superintendent said ductile pipe is not a huge cost difference over plastic and delivery looks better; pipe purchase is substantial.
The state funding was changed to a grant rather than a loan or principal forgiveness, so approved work is paid for; an article is still needed to authorize spending.
A member noted costs before approval would come from the regular maintenance budget.

decisions.decision: Applicant must resubmit signed petitions with a formal written request to expand the district before the board can call a special meeting.
Discussion of the Bird Street project closed; applicants and residents will be notified when an application arrives and it will be posted on the agenda.
Superintendent offered to prepare water-demand calculations, including a worst-case scenario, for an interested resident.
The grant-acceptance article will stay as drafted pending word from town counsel, and the engineering agreement can be signed now.
Board will consider scheduling meetings later in the day if enough residents want it.

what_happened.line: Water commissioners spent most of the meeting hearing residents on a request to expand the water district to a Bird Street site; no petition has been filed and no vote was taken.
The board said the applicant must resubmit signed petitions with a formal written request before a special meeting can be called.
Discussion of the Bird Street project closed; applicants and residents will be notified when an application arrives, and it will be posted on the agenda.
The board moved to let the superintendent and chairman sign the lead service line replacement paperwork; the result was not audible in the recording.
The grant-acceptance article will stay as drafted pending word from town counsel, and the engineering agreement can be signed now.

why_it_matters: Expanding the water district needs a vote of the district, so residents may be asked to decide whether public water extends to a new development site.
Residents raised contamination, PFAS testing and private-well effects; none of those questions was settled, and the minutes show nothing binding the developers to their proposed figures.
The lead service line funding is now a grant, so approved work is paid for, but an article is still needed to authorize spending.
watch_next: A formal written request with signed petitions from the applicant, which would be posted on a future agenda.
The town counsel answer on the grant-acceptance article and the lead service line spending article.
